proof_boundary: This proves the exact transport profiles, closed rho-v operator, saddle zero, carrier-ridge trace, hyperbolic phase and boost, finite transverse kernel, and ideal derivative and terminal identities. It proves no signed ridge-completed ideal join, transverse residual bound, far aggregate, completed current, Phi_B theorem, contact exclusion, retained aggregate or Xi theorem, Lambda<=0, PF-infinity, RH, or prize-level conclusion.

rows.certificate: Define h(w)=w-1-log w, mathfrak R(w)=2h(w)/(w-1), and mathfrak B(w)=2h(w)/(w-1)^2, with removable values mathfrak R(1)=0 and mathfrak B(1)=1. Also z(w)J(w)=w mathfrak R(w).
rows.claim: Two removable scalar profiles control the transport.

rows.certificate: The exact logarithmic Jacobian identity is zJ partial_w log J=1-mathfrak B(w). It converts the weighted flux transport into two elementary profile functions.
rows.claim: The Morse Jacobian derivative reduces to mathfrak B.

rows.certificate: At w=1+d, mathfrak R=d-2d^2/3+d^3/2-2d^4/5+..., while mathfrak B=1-2d/3+d^2/2-2d^3/5+d^4/3+.... Thus the transport has a removable first-order zero at the double saddle.
rows.claim: The transport profiles have explicit removable saddle series.

rows.certificate: mathfrak B(w)>0 for w>0, while mathfrak R(w) has the sign of w-1. A coefficient-blind ridge transport therefore changes orientation across the reciprocal saddle.
rows.claim: The ridge profile reverses sign across the saddle.
rows.proof_boundary: This is not a physical current sign.

rows.certificate: The boundary-flux transport vector is mathcal L=eta partial_eta-y partial_y=z(rho)J(rho)partial_rho-z(v)J(v)partial_v.
rows.claim: The weighted flux interior has an exact rho-v vector field.

rows.certificate: For G_P=exp(S(x))P(x)J(rho)J(v)/rho, x=log(pv/rho), the exact identity is mathcal L G_P=exp(S)J(rho)J(v)/rho times {[mathfrak B(v)-mathfrak B(rho)-mathfrak R(rho)]P-[mathfrak R(rho)+mathfrak R(v)](P'+gP)}.
rows.claim: The complete transport reduces to P and P'+gP with explicit profiles.

rows.certificate: At rho=v=1 both coefficients vanish. To first order they are -(delta_rho+2delta_v)/3 and -(delta_rho+delta_v), so the interior transport gains one local displacement but not two.
rows.claim: Both transport coefficients vanish at the double saddle.

rows.certificate: On the carrier ridge v=rho, mathcal L G_P=-exp(S(log p))J(rho)^2 mathfrak R(rho){P+2(P'+gP)}(log p)/rho. The phase is constant there, so this trace must be recombined with the returned carrier rather than bounded as an oscillatory cell error.
rows.claim: The exact ridge transport has constant phase and a live coefficient.
rows.proof_boundary: It must remain joined to returned carriers.

rows.certificate: Put s=(eta+y)/sqrt(2) and d=(eta-y)/sqrt(2). Then (eta^2-y^2)/2=sd and deta dy has unit absolute Jacobian.
rows.claim: An orthogonal change gives phase sd.
rows.proof_boundary: The domain remains finite and curved.

rows.certificate: The transport becomes mathcal L=d partial_s+s partial_d. It differentiates transversely on the carrier ridge d=0, where the phase e(sd) is constant.
rows.claim: The transport is the hyperbolic boost d partial_s+s partial_d.

rows.certificate: For fixed s!=0 and finite transverse limits d_-<d_+, integral_(d_-)^(d_+)e(sd)dd=kappa{e(sd_+)-e(sd_-)}/s, with removable value d_+-d_- at s=0. This is the exact finite transverse Fourier kernel.
rows.claim: The finite d integral has an exact removable 1/s kernel.
rows.proof_boundary: The central s chart remains explicit.

rows.certificate: Subtract the ridge amplitude before estimating the transverse residual. For |s| away from zero, integrate the residual in d with the exact 1/s kernel; keep a central s-neighborhood and reciprocal side traces joined to the returned carrier. A two-dimensional modulus would erase this structure.
rows.claim: Ridge subtraction precedes transverse estimation.

rows.certificate: The exact ideal derivatives are (P_H^0)'=-i(x-u_N)(3x+u_N)/4 and (P_T^0)'=-i(x+u_N)(3x-u_N)/4+u_(N,x). They enter the transport only through P'+gP.
rows.claim: Both cubic derivative rows are explicit.

rows.certificate: At x=-u_N, P_H^0=0 but (P_H^0)'=-iu_N^2. Also P_T^0=-2u_Nu_(N,x) and (P_T^0)'+g_NP_T^0=u_(N,x)(1-2g_Nu_N). Thus the Hermitian value null does not delete the terminal-neighborhood interior transport.
rows.claim: The Hermitian value null leaves derivative transport.
rows.proof_boundary: The transpose terminal quadrature remains joined.

rows.certificate: Neither P_H^0+2{(P_H^0)'+gP_H^0} nor its transpose analogue vanishes identically. The nonoscillatory ridge transport is therefore a live joined-carrier term, not a polynomial null.
rows.claim: Neither ideal ridge coefficient vanishes identically.

rows.certificate: mathfrak B(w)>0 for w>0, while mathfrak R(w) has the sign of w-1. A coefficient-blind ridge transport therefore changes orientation across the reciprocal saddle.
rows.claim: The constant source ridge transport changes sign with rho-1.

Then split the residual into a central |s| chart and an outer transverse 1/s kernel, keeping physical rails, reciprocal sides, and far compression joined.
rows.claim: Compose the exact ridge with both returned carriers.
